hardware_freedoms.status: A concatenated sequence of complete rows with the same input is an ordinary GEMV. Inactive rows may be overread/computed and discarded, with all actual costs charged.

hardware_freedoms.status: diag(A,B) times concatenate(xA,xB) equals concatenate(AxA,BxB), using an ordinary dense GEMV. The zero entries, larger input, inactive-partner work and outputs are real costs.

Small fringes may share a wave by paying structural zeros; complete full-wave tiles cannot gain because two-way block diagonal doubles useful-byte volume. minimum_work_atomization.notation: W=65536 byte four-plane ordinary-read wave; C INT8 bytes per complete output row; R output rows; r_c whole-row chip shards; sum r_c=R.
minimum_work_atomization.cost: Q=sum_c ceil(r_c*C/W). Byte-work lower bound Q>=ceil(R*C/W).
minimum_work_atomization.lemma_scope: R*C is an integer multiple of W; all weights are read densely, without zero expansion or alternative arithmetic.
minimum_work_atomization.lemma: Q=R*C/W iff every nonempty shard has r_c*C divisible by W. Equivalently r_c is a multiple of r0=W/gcd(W,C).
minimum_work_atomization.proof: Every ceiling contributes nonnegative rounding loss. Since total exact byte work is integral, equality requires each rounding loss to vanish; the divisibility condition follows from gcd. Conversely these aligned shards have zero rounding loss.
minimum_work_atomization.atom: r0 complete rows require q0=C/gcd(W,C) waves. Work-minimal placement is fixed-atom placement with additive q0 cost; atoms from the same expert on a chip can be joined into legal whole-row runs, charging block crossings.
minimum_work_atomization.implication: A minimum-work compiler is a useful correctness/cost certification pass, but choosing these atoms and applying weighted query minmax declustering is not a new optimization principle. A publication claim needs a demonstrable issue outside that reduction and a matched strong baseline.
potential_nonadditive_extensions: Deliberately pay extra waves to increase fanout and reduce critical path. Parent mixed-width screens report negligible additional gains; no new claim here.
Same-input adjacency/run merging, compared against Neuralink-style access collapse.
Different-input block-diagonal padding, with explicit capacity/ECC/MAC/input/output charges.

granite4_row_phase_obstacle.candidate: Flatten each g16 GU shard of64rows×1536 into6 dense16KiB pages; adjacent experts share a middle WL.
granite4_row_phase_obstacle.conditional_correctness_statement: For a row-major concatenated stream, an ordinary dense GEMV must begin on an original row boundary. Merely reading all bytes of a WL and discarding fringe outputs does not fix a start inside a row: all subsequent dot-product column phases remain displaced.
granite4_row_phase_obstacle.published_abi_check: Personally reread original AiF Fig14 and §4.4 p536: one SREG; input dimension, block ID, block offset and page count; input loaded into PBs. §5.2 locates submatrix start page addresses. No prefix-skip, input-column-phase, per-plane offset list or fragment accumulation operand is documented.
granite4_row_phase_obstacle.unresolved: The meaning of block offset is not specified enough to prove that a logical stream can start at plane2 and consume a row-aligned6-page interval without new chip behavior. Do not declare this impossible; do not assume the needed behavior is provided.
granite4_row_phase_obstacle.safe_full_WL_case: If only full-WL row-major runs with no prefix support are admitted, valid boundaries repeat every3WL. An isolated64-row expert then expands to its128-row/3WL pair, recovering the old overread-bundle cost rather than the optimistic2WL union.
granite4_row_phase_obstacle.different_model_control: DeepSeek GU has2048-byte rows dividing64KiB, so the specific WL-row-phase obstacle disappears. Its22-page g16 shard is5.5WL; even perfect top6 pairing saves at most3/36=8.333% GU NAND waves before full-cost/strong-layout comparisons.

bound_derivation: There are 15 per-expert chip jobs before fringe coactivation; top6 gives 90 jobs.
A selected pair in the fixed quarter-fringe pairing graph saves exactly one job. Each expert has four fringes, so its graph degree is four; repeated expert pairs are permitted.
For max chip load <=5, total jobs must be <=16*5=80, requiring at least ten coactive pairs on that query.
Thus P(max_load<=5) <= E[pairs]/10 by Markov. Also max_load>=5 since even twelve coactive pairs leave 78 jobs. E[max_load]>=6-E[pairs]/10.
The degree-at-most-four fractional matching LP maximizes expected coactive pairs using training pair frequencies. Dropping integer, chip, and placement constraints makes it an upper bound.
Explicit nonnegative dual vertex prices certify each edge weight <= sum of endpoint prices; four times sum of prices is an expected-pairs upper bound.
This lower bound ignores block splitting, ECC/MAC work on zeros, inactive-row outputs, input concatenation, inactive partner input slots and gang readiness. They cannot improve this NAND lower bound.

uniform_control.reason: Every four-regular multigraph has 128 edges; uniform top6 coactivation frequency is 30/(64*63).

blockdiag_fringe_screen.verdict: NO-GO for this exact 11-full/4-quarter/1-empty family on the frozen training screen: even the relaxed NAND bound loses to frozen g12.
blockdiag_fringe_screen.falsifiable_gate: Before any physical fit, candidate NAND lower bound must beat frozen g12 on training; it failed in all40layers. Changing geometry requires a new bound, not reusing this no-go as a universal result.
blockdiag_fringe_screen.validation: LP primal degrees checked; explicit nonnegative vertex-price dual certificate satisfies every edge constraint after conservative numerical repair. Fixed-top6 control reaches12pairs; uniform control equals128×30/(64×63). No heldout, weights or author sources changed.

compiler_novelty_assessment.concrete_problem_if_reopened: Jointly choose complete-row shards and legal same-input dense read intervals with explicit block/WL row-phase compatibility, structural-zero alternatives, native input/output bytes and bounded storage. This is more concrete than a generic hypergraph label, but the new mechanisms still need positive headroom and distinctions from existing packing/coalescing.
compiler_novelty_assessment.current_no_go: Do not propose a new general NAND configuration compiler solely by composing gcd atomization, ordinary bin packing and a query-aware hypergraph solver. Existing favorable examples so far are baseline corrections or narrow shape gains, not evidence that the missing compiler itself enables substantial new performance.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A fully legal interval/row map whose measured or calibrated gain survives same-geometry declustering and same-overread coalescing controls.
A different existing-hardware geometry showing a material achievable gap after relaxed work/capacity bounds; no such instance established in this task.

compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.parent_proposal: 64 experts×12 canonical full-wave down tiles;16 chips; any top6 must finish within5 waves/chip. Parent constructed688extra tile copies via20special experts each forbidding one nondefault omission color.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.initial_check: No counterexample found to the stated color-Hall sufficiency: every color is forbidden by only5experts, and each expert forbids at most one color. In any selected6, each color has an eligible expert; any>=2-color subset has all6 selected experts as neighbors. Thus four distinct expert representatives can cover the four colors. Two remaining experts can choose different available colors, obtaining2/2/1/1.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.lower_bound_scope: With fixed full-wave private-expert canonical tiles, any chip can own at most5 unreplicated tiles; any6 such tiles have at most6 expert owners and can be included in one top6 request. Hence extra copies>=768−16×5=688.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.strong_primary_prior: Bujtás–Tuza2012 formalizes replica-only batch retrieval via relaxed Hall conditions. Its singleton restriction and2n−mt storage-counting form are direct prior to this style of lower bound. Their arbitrary-atomic-query upper constructions do not automatically prove the present compound-query construction.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.not_directly_same_problem: Conventional CBC requires arbitrary requested atomic-item subsets; here a query includes all12tiles of each of6experts. Exact688construction for this family was not located in the bounded search. This absence is not novelty clearance.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.withdrawn_generalization: A suggested bytewise extension counting ceil(unreplicated_expert_bytes/W) separately per expert is not generally valid when block-diagonal padding and input concatenation are admitted. Two32-row×512-byte fringes can be stored as a64-row×1024-byte block diagonal and computed in one full wave. Keep canonical/private-expert-wave scope unless a stronger proof explicitly handles structural zeros.
compound_replica_theorem_prior_audit.performance_limit: Parent reports only about1–3% whole routed-FFN opportunity for the current G4 case; this task does not label the theorem or system a breakthrough.
